Experiment: Outbox Sequence Gap Anomaly under Concurrent External Transactions
Session1Action: UPDATE Account 1 -> allocated seq_id=1, stayed uncommitted
Session2Action: UPDATE Account 2 -> allocated seq_id=2, committed immediately
OperationalConclusion: This confirms experimentally that a scalar sequence watermark (WHERE seq_id > @lastSeq) silently and permanently drops committed mutations whenever concurrent external transactions commit out of sequence order.

StrictCoordinatorMode.Policy: All mutating traffic MUST route through EapCoordinator.UpdateAccountAsync under the global advisory lock.
StrictCoordinatorMode.Enforcement: REVOKE INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON accounts FROM PUBLIC, application_role; GRANT to coordinator_role ONLY.
StrictCoordinatorMode.Guarantee: Strict serial commit ordering, zero sequence gaps, zero stale reads on coordinator path.

EventualExternalMode.Policy: If external SQL writes must be permitted, the outbox poller CANNOT use a simple scalar watermark.
EventualExternalMode.RequiredFix: Must deploy PostgreSQL Logical Replication (pgoutput WAL decoding) or a sliding confirmation window that only advances across contiguous committed sequence numbers.
